title: NDA Strategizes to Sweep All Eight Bihar Legislative Council Seats on October 23
excerpt: A Wednesday huddle at the CM's residence sought to douse internal rebellions before the October 9 nomination-withdrawal deadline — while the opposition's own seat-sharing frictions hand the alliance an opening.
body:
• The NDA's senior leadership met at Chief Minister Samrat Chaudhary's Patna residence on Wednesday to lock a joint campaign plan for all eight Bihar Legislative Council seats going to polls on October 23.
  • BJP and JD(U) are contesting four seats each; a follow-up meeting of the full NDA legislative party — MLAs, MLCs and alliance MPs — is scheduled for Friday, October 9 to give the strategy its final shape.
  • Internal frictions dominated the talks: JD(U) MLA Anant Singh is backing a rival candidate against his own party's nominee in Patna Graduates, and a smaller NDA ally is running against JD(U) in Saran Teachers.
  • Eligibility check: only registered graduate voters with a recognized degree at least three years old can vote in the graduates' constituencies; polling is October 23 from 8 am to 4 pm, with counting on October 27.

A Wednesday Huddle at the CM's Residence

Bihar's ruling National Democratic Alliance moved to put its house in order this week, with senior leaders of all constituent parties gathering at Chief Minister Samrat Chaudhary's official residence in Patna on Wednesday to thrash out a common strategy for the October 23 elections to eight Legislative Council seats. The eight seats — four from graduates' constituencies and four from teachers' constituencies — are among the few electoral contests where India's educated electorate votes directly, and both the ruling alliance and the opposition are treating them as a bellwether.

https://x.com/ANI/status/2108553502494712305

The meeting drew the alliance's heavyweights: JD(U) national working president Sanjay Jha, Deputy Chief Minister Vijay Kumar Chaudhary, ministers Bijendra Prasad Yadav and Santosh Kumar Suman, BJP state president Sanjay Saraogi, and JD(U) state president Umesh Singh Kushwaha. The NDA currently holds five of the eight seats, and all five sitting MLCs — four of them from the BJP — are seeking re-election.

Unity Message, With an Eye on Rebels

The public messaging was all about unity. Chaudhary told leaders that the alliance, not individual parties, must be the priority during the campaign, and urged joint participation of leaders and workers from every constituent in support of the eight official candidates. Saraogi told reporters afterward that the NDA would fight the elections "together as a team."

But much of Wednesday's closed-door discussion was about the cracks. In the Patna Graduates constituency, JD(U)'s candidate Neeraj Kumar faces a bizarre revolt from within: his own party's Mokama MLA, Anant Singh, has openly backed Jan Suraaj candidate Anuj Singh and vowed to ensure Kumar's defeat. In the Saran Teachers seat, JD(U) candidate Anand Pushkar faces competition from Ram Pukar Sinha of the Rashtriya Lok Morcha, the smallest constituent of the ruling alliance itself.

"The NDA is intact and stands united. As far as issues concerning individual parties are concerned, respective state party presidents have been empowered to take appropriate action."

— Sanjay Saraogi, BJP state president, Bihar

The meeting's answer was procedural: each party's leadership would resolve its own internal disputes, and NDA leaders would hold direct talks with allied-party figures running against official candidates. The timing matters — October 9 is the deadline for withdrawal of nominations, and the leadership wants friendly fire eliminated before that window closes so official candidates can campaign with the alliance's full weight behind them.

Why These Seats Matter

Legislative Council elections from graduates' and teachers' constituencies are a peculiar Indian institution: only registered graduates (with a degree at least three years old, ordinarily resident in the constituency) and registered teachers can vote. Turnout is small and organized, which makes these contests unusually sensitive to party machinery — and to rebel candidates who can peel off a few hundred votes.

That is why the opposition's disarray matters as much as the NDA's. The RJD announced candidates for six seats and the Congress for five — four of them directly overlapping RJD nominees, in what leaders first described as a "friendly fight" and what has since turned into an open tiff. Jan Suraaj has fielded candidates too, including Dr Anuj Singh in Patna Graduates, who is getting Anant Singh's support. With multi-cornered contests expected across all eight seats, split opposition votes could be the NDA's biggest asset.

What Comes Next

Friday's legislative-party meeting will be the final checkpoint before campaigning intensifies: all NDA MLAs, MLCs, and alliance MPs have been called to the Chief Minister's residence to finalize the campaign plan. JD(U)'s Umesh Kushwaha has already declared the result a foregone conclusion, telling IANS the NDA would secure a "one-sided victory" on all eight seats, citing the alliance's performance in the 2025 Assembly elections.

The real test is whether the internal fires get doused by the October 9 withdrawal deadline. If Anant Singh stays in the field against Neeraj Kumar, the Patna Graduates contest could embarrass the ruling alliance even in a sweep — a reminder that in Bihar, the fiercest fights are often fought within, not between, the coalitions.
